system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Charles Schwab (SCHW) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Charles Schwab Trading Activity Index increased to 48.75 in November, up from its score of 48.12 in October

BODY:
The only index of its kind, the STAX is a proprietary, behavior-based index that analyzes retail investor stock positions and trading activity from Schwab's millions of client accounts to illuminate what investors were actually doing and how they were positioned in the markets each month.The government shutdown that began in October and continued into November meant investors had to rely on private sector labor market data, all of which showed slowing economic and consumer sentiment. Major indexes spent much of November losing ground amid weakness in Magnificent Seven names and cryptocurrencies, hurt partly by falling hopes for a December rate cut by the Federal Reserve. However, the market got a significant boost toward the end of the month when New York Federal Reserve President John Williams signaled a preference for a rate cut in December, bringing the likelihood of a cut from a low of 40% into the high-80s according to the CME FedWatch Tool. 
As in October, the most aggressively positioned investors tracked by Schwab during November again belonged to Generation X, born between 1965 and 1980. Among the least aggressive was Generation Z, born between 1997 and 2012. 
Popular names bought by Schwab clients during the period included: NVIDIA Corp. (NVDA), Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR), Meta Platforms Inc. (META), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) and Tesla Inc. (TSLA). 
Names net sold by Schwab clients during the period included: Apple Inc. (AAPL), Broadcom Inc. (AVGO), Eli Lilly and Co. (LLY), Intel Corp. (INTC) and Rivian Automotive Inc. (RIVN).
</article>

<summary>
[SCHW relevance: primary | sentiment: neutral]
Schwab's proprietary STAX index, tracking retail client trading behavior, fell to 48.75 in November from 48.12 in October, indicating slightly more aggressive positioning amid volatile markets and shifting Fed rate-raised expectations.
Key facts:
- STAX fell to 48.75 in November from 48.12 in October
- Generation X most aggressively positioned; Generation Z least aggressive
- Clients bought NVDA, PLTR, META, AMZN, TSLA; sold AAPL, AVGO, LLY, INTC, RIVN
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to SCHW)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about SCHW in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a SCHW analyst what matters, and represent how central SCHW really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for SCHW, and says so plainly if SCHW is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the SCHW angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores SCHW, or implies the article is about / important for SCHW when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
